    dpi=300,
)

const OUTDIR = joinpath(@__DIR__, "output", "comparison")
mkpath(OUTDIR)

# ============================================================================
# Tier 1: Oregonator — Full Quantitative Comparison
# ============================================================================
function run_oregonator_comparison()
    println("=" ^ 60)
    println("TIER 1: Oregonator — Full Quantitative Comparison")
    println("=" ^ 60)

    rn = @reaction_network begin
        @species X(t) Y(t) Z(t)
        @parameters k1 k2 k3 k4 k5
        k1, Y --> X
        k2, X + Y --> 0
        k3, X --> 2X + Z
        k4, 2X --> 0
        k5, Z --> Y
    end

    y1s, y2s, y3s = 500.0, 1000.0, 2000.0
    mu1s, mu2s = 2000.0, 50000.0
    rates = [
        mu1s / y2s,
        mu2s / (y1s * y2s),
        (mu1s + mu2s) / y1s,
        2 * mu1s / y1s^2,
        (mu1s + mu2s) / y3s,
    ]

    tfinal = 0.11
    prob = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(500, 1000, 2000), (0.0, tfinal), rates;
                      bounds=(0, 50_000))

    # Run AdaptiveFSP
    println("\nRunning AdaptiveFSP...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_afsp_start = time()
    sol_afsp = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(
        ε_dt=1.0, prob_quantile=0.1, flux_tolerance=1.0,
        expansion_depth=1, save_interval=1000,
    ))
    t_afsp = time() - t_afsp_start
    traj_afsp = mean_trajectory(sol_afsp)

    # Run KrylovFSP
    println("\nRunning KrylovFSP...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_kfsp_start = time()
    sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp = solve(prob, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-3, τ_init=1e-3, ℓ=5, r=1, save_interval=1000,
    ))
    t_kfsp = time() - t_kfsp_start
    traj_kfsp = mean_trajectory(sol_kfsp)

    # Print results table
    println("\n--- Oregonator Results ---")
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15s  %15s", "", "AdaptiveFSP", "KrylovFSP"))
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15.2f  %15.2f", "Wall time (s)", t_afsp, t_kfsp))
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15d  %15d", "Snapshots", length(sol_afsp), length(sol_kfsp)))
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15d  %15d", "Final |S|",
            sol_afsp.state_space_sizes[end], sol_kfsp.state_space_sizes[end]))
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15d  %15d", "Max |S|",
            maximum(sol_afsp.state_space_sizes), maximum(sol_kfsp.state_space_sizes)))
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15d", "KrylovFSP rejections", diag_kfsp.reject_count))
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15d", "KrylovFSP total iters", diag_kfsp.total_iters))

    # Generate plots
    # (a) Mean trajectories overlaid
    p1 = plot(title="(a) Mean trajectories", xlabel="Time", ylabel="Population")
    plot!(p1, sol_afsp.t, traj_afsp[:, 1], label="X (AdaptiveFSP)", color=:blue, linestyle=:solid)
    plot!(p1, sol_afsp.t, traj_afsp[:, 2], label="Y (AdaptiveFSP)", color=:red, linestyle=:solid)
    plot!(p1, sol_afsp.t, traj_afsp[:, 3], label="Z (AdaptiveFSP)", color=:green, linestyle=:solid)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p1, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 1], label="X (KrylovFSP)", color=:blue, linestyle=:dash)
        plot!(p1, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 2], label="Y (KrylovFSP)", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
        plot!(p1, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 3], label="Z (KrylovFSP)", color=:green, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    # (b) State space size over time
    p2 = plot(title="(b) State space size", xlabel="Time", ylabel="|S|")
    plot!(p2, sol_afsp.t, sol_afsp.state_space_sizes, label="AdaptiveFSP", color=:blue)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p2, sol_kfsp.t, sol_kfsp.state_space_sizes, label="KrylovFSP", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    # (c) dt/τ over time
    p3 = plot(title="(c) Time step size", xlabel="Time", ylabel="dt / τ", yscale=:log10)
    if length(sol_afsp.t) > 1
        dt_afsp = diff(sol_afsp.t)
        plot!(p3, sol_afsp.t[2:end], dt_afsp, label="AdaptiveFSP dt", color=:blue)
    end
    if length(diag_kfsp.τ_log) > 0
        plot!(p3, diag_kfsp.time_log, diag_kfsp.τ_log, label="KrylovFSP τ", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    # (d) Marginal distribution at final time
    p4 = plot(title="(d) Marginal P(X) at t_f", xlabel="X", ylabel="Probability")
    if length(sol_afsp) > 0
        m_afsp = marginal(sol_afsp, length(sol_afsp), 1)
        bar!(p4, m_afsp.values, m_afsp.probs, label="AdaptiveFSP", alpha=0.5, color=:blue)
    end
    if length(sol_kfsp) > 0
        m_kfsp = marginal(sol_kfsp, length(sol_kfsp), 1)
        bar!(p4, m_kfsp.values, m_kfsp.probs, label="KrylovFSP", alpha=0.5, color=:red)
    end

    fig = plot(p1, p2, p3, p4; layout=(2, 2), size=(1200, 800), margin=5Plots.mm)
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "oregonator_comparison.png"))
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "oregonator_comparison.pdf"))
    println("Saved oregonator_comparison.{png,pdf}")

    return (sol_afsp=sol_afsp, sol_kfsp=sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp=diag_kfsp,
            t_afsp=t_afsp, t_kfsp=t_kfsp)
end

"""
    KrylovFSP(; kwargs...)

Krylov-FSP-SSA baseline algorithm (Sidje & Vo 2015, reviewed in Dinh & Sidje 2016).

Uses probability-threshold pruning (no flux protection), mass-conservation
accept/reject time stepping, and SSA-driven + reachability expansion.

# Keyword Arguments
- `ε::Float64 = 1e-3`: Total probability mass loss tolerance.
- `τ_init::Float64 = 1.0`: Initial time step.
- `prob_threshold::Float64 = 0.0`: Hard probability threshold for pruning (0 = use ε/|S|).
- `ℓ::Int = 5`: Lookback window length for max-probability tracking.
- `r::Int = 1`: Reachability expansion depth after SSA.
- `save_interval::Int = 1000`: Save a snapshot every N iterations.
- `max_iter::Int = typemax(Int)`: Maximum number of iterations (for diagnostic runs).
"""
Base.@kwdef struct KrylovFSP
    ε::Float64 = 1e-3
    τ_init::Float64 = 1.0
    prob_threshold::Float64 = 0.0
    ℓ::Int = 5
    r::Int = 1
    save_interval::Int = 1000
    max_iter::Int = typemax(Int)
end

"""
    KrylovFSPDiagnostics

Per-iteration diagnostic data from a KrylovFSP solve.
"""
struct KrylovFSPDiagnostics
    τ_log::Vector{Float64}
    mass_log::Vector{Float64}
    time_log::Vector{Float64}
    walltime_log::Vector{Float64}
    size_log::Vector{Int}
    reject_count::Int
    total_iters::Int
end

"""
    solve(prob::FSPProblem, alg::KrylovFSP) -> (FSPSolution, KrylovFSPDiagnostics)

Run the Krylov-FSP-SSA algorithm (Dinh & Sidje 2016, Algorithm [18]).

Returns a tuple of `(solution, diagnostics)` where diagnostics contains
per-iteration τ, mass, timing, and rejection data for failure-mode analysis.
"""
function CommonSolve.solve(prob::FSPProblem{E,T}, alg::KrylovFSP) where {E,T}
    model = prob.model
    rates = prob.rates
    bc = prob.bc
    t0, tf = prob.tspan
    n_species = length(Tuple(prob.u0))

    # Initialize state space
    sp = StateSpace{E, Float64}()
    add_state!(sp, prob.u0, 1.0)

    # Solution storage
    sol_t = Float64[t0]
    sol_snaps = [(copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs))]
    sol_sizes = [length(sp)]

    # Diagnostics
    τ_log = Float64[]
    mass_log = Float64[]
    time_log = Float64[]
    walltime_log = Float64[]
    size_log = Int[]
    reject_count = 0

    # Lookback window for max-probability tracking
    prob_history = Vector{Dict{E,Float64}}()

    t = Float64(t0)
    τ = Float64(alg.τ_init)
    iter = 0
    wall_start = time()

    while t < tf && iter < alg.max_iter
        iter += 1

        # Determine pruning threshold
        threshold = alg.prob_threshold > 0 ? alg.prob_threshold : alg.ε / max(length(sp), 1)

        # Update lookback window
        current_probs = Dict{E,Float64}(s => sp.probs[sp.index[s]] for s in sp.states)
        push!(prob_history, current_probs)
        if length(prob_history) > alg.ℓ
            popfirst!(prob_history)
        end

        # Compute max probability over lookback window
        max_probs = Dict{E,Float64}()
        for hist in prob_history
            for (s, p) in hist
                max_probs[s] = max(get(max_probs, s, 0.0), p)
            end
        end

        # 1. Threshold prune (with lookback protection)
        prune_threshold!(sp, threshold; max_probs=max_probs)

        # 2. SSA-driven expansion
        expand_ssa!(sp, model, rates, t, bc; depth=1)

        # 3. r-step reachability expansion
        if alg.r > 0
            expand!(sp, model, bc; depth=alg.r)
        end

        # 4. Build generator + propagate
        τ_step = min(τ, tf - t)
        A, _, _ = build_generator(sp, model, rates, t)
        p_new = expmv(τ_step, A, sp.probs)

        # 5. Accept/reject based on mass conservation
        mass = sum(p_new)
        mass_target = 1.0 - alg.ε * (t + τ_step) / tf

        if mass >= mass_target
            # Accept step
            sp.probs = p_new
            t += τ_step

            push!(τ_log, τ_step)
            push!(mass_log, mass)
            push!(time_log, t)
            push!(walltime_log, time() - wall_start)
            push!(size_log, length(sp))

            # Save snapshot
            if iter % alg.save_interval == 0 || t >= tf
                push!(sol_t, t)
                push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
                push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
                @info "KrylovFSP: t = $(round(t; sigdigits=4)), |S| = $(length(sp)), τ = $(round(τ_step; sigdigits=3)), mass = $(round(mass; sigdigits=6))"
            end
        else
            # Reject: halve τ
            τ /= 2
            reject_count += 1

            push!(τ_log, τ_step)
            push!(mass_log, mass)
            push!(time_log, t)
            push!(walltime_log, time() - wall_start)
            push!(size_log, length(sp))

            if iter % alg.save_interval == 0
                @info "KrylovFSP REJECT: t = $(round(t; sigdigits=4)), τ = $(round(τ; sigdigits=3)), mass = $(round(mass; sigdigits=6))"
            end
        end
    end

    # Ensure final snapshot is captured
    if sol_t[end] < t
        push!(sol_t, t)
        push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
        push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
    end

    sol = FSPSolution{E}(sol_t, sol_snaps, sol_sizes, n_species)
    diag = KrylovFSPDiagnostics(τ_log, mass_log, time_log, walltime_log, size_log, reject_count, iter)

    (sol, diag)
end

"""
    KrylovFSP(; kwargs...)

Krylov-FSP-SSA baseline algorithm (Sidje & Vo 2015, reviewed in Dinh & Sidje 2016).

Uses probability-threshold pruning (no flux protection), mass-conservation
accept/reject time stepping, and SSA-driven + reachability expansion.

# Keyword Arguments
- `ε::Float64 = 1e-3`: Total probability mass loss tolerance.
- `τ_init::Float64 = 1.0`: Initial time step.
- `prob_threshold::Float64 = 0.0`: Hard probability threshold for pruning (0 = use ε/|S|).
- `ℓ::Int = 5`: Lookback window length for max-probability tracking.
- `r::Int = 1`: Reachability expansion depth after SSA.
- `save_interval::Int = 1000`: Save a snapshot every N iterations.
- `max_iter::Int = typemax(Int)`: Maximum number of iterations (for diagnostic runs).
"""
Base.@kwdef struct KrylovFSP
    ε::Float64 = 1e-3
    τ_init::Float64 = 1.0
    prob_threshold::Float64 = 0.0
    ℓ::Int = 5
    r::Int = 1
    save_interval::Int = 1000
    max_iter::Int = typemax(Int)
end

"""
    KrylovFSPDiagnostics

Per-iteration diagnostic data from a KrylovFSP solve.
"""
struct KrylovFSPDiagnostics
    τ_log::Vector{Float64}
    mass_log::Vector{Float64}
    time_log::Vector{Float64}
    walltime_log::Vector{Float64}
    size_log::Vector{Int}
    reject_count::Int
    total_iters::Int
end

"""
    solve(prob::FSPProblem, alg::KrylovFSP) -> (FSPSolution, KrylovFSPDiagnostics)

Run the Krylov-FSP-SSA algorithm (Dinh & Sidje 2016, Algorithm [18]).

Returns a tuple of `(solution, diagnostics)` where diagnostics contains
per-iteration τ, mass, timing, and rejection data for failure-mode analysis.
"""
function CommonSolve.solve(prob::FSPProblem{E,T}, alg::KrylovFSP) where {E,T}
    model = prob.model
    rates = prob.rates
    bc = prob.bc
    t0, tf = prob.tspan
    n_species = length(Tuple(prob.u0))

    # Initialize state space
    sp = StateSpace{E, Float64}()
    add_state!(sp, prob.u0, 1.0)

    # Solution storage
    sol_t = Float64[t0]
    sol_snaps = [(copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs))]
    sol_sizes = [length(sp)]

    # Diagnostics
    τ_log = Float64[]
    mass_log = Float64[]
    time_log = Float64[]
    walltime_log = Float64[]
    size_log = Int[]
    reject_count = 0

    # Lookback window for max-probability tracking
    prob_history = Vector{Dict{E,Float64}}()

    t = Float64(t0)
    τ = Float64(alg.τ_init)
    iter = 0
    wall_start = time()

    while t < tf && iter < alg.max_iter
        iter += 1

        # Determine pruning threshold
        threshold = alg.prob_threshold > 0 ? alg.prob_threshold : alg.ε / max(length(sp), 1)

        # Update lookback window
        current_probs = Dict{E,Float64}(s => sp.probs[sp.index[s]] for s in sp.states)
        push!(prob_history, current_probs)
        if length(prob_history) > alg.ℓ
            popfirst!(prob_history)
        end

        # Compute max probability over lookback window
        max_probs = Dict{E,Float64}()
        for hist in prob_history
            for (s, p) in hist
                max_probs[s] = max(get(max_probs, s, 0.0), p)
            end
        end

        # 1. Threshold prune (with lookback protection)
        prune_threshold!(sp, threshold; max_probs=max_probs)

        # 2. SSA-driven expansion
        expand_ssa!(sp, model, rates, t, bc; depth=1)

        # 3. r-step reachability expansion
        if alg.r > 0
            expand!(sp, model, bc; depth=alg.r)
        end

        # 4. Build generator + propagate
        τ_step = min(τ, tf - t)
        A, _, _ = build_generator(sp, model, rates, t)
        p_new = expmv(τ_step, A, sp.probs)

        # 5. Accept/reject based on mass conservation
        mass = sum(p_new)
        mass_target = 1.0 - alg.ε * (t + τ_step) / tf

        if mass >= mass_target
            # Accept step
            sp.probs = p_new
            t += τ_step

            push!(τ_log, τ_step)
            push!(mass_log, mass)
            push!(time_log, t)
            push!(walltime_log, time() - wall_start)
            push!(size_log, length(sp))

            # Save snapshot
            if iter % alg.save_interval == 0 || t >= tf
                push!(sol_t, t)
                push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
                push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
                @info "KrylovFSP: t = $(round(t; sigdigits=4)), |S| = $(length(sp)), τ = $(round(τ_step; sigdigits=3)), mass = $(round(mass; sigdigits=6))"
            end
        else
            # Reject: halve τ
            τ /= 2
            reject_count += 1

            push!(τ_log, τ_step)
            push!(mass_log, mass)
            push!(time_log, t)
            push!(walltime_log, time() - wall_start)
            push!(size_log, length(sp))

            if iter % alg.save_interval == 0
                @info "KrylovFSP REJECT: t = $(round(t; sigdigits=4)), τ = $(round(τ; sigdigits=3)), mass = $(round(mass; sigdigits=6))"
            end
        end
    end

    # Ensure final snapshot is captured (avoid duplicate if already saved in loop)
    if length(sol_t) == 1 || sol_t[end] < t - eps(t)
        push!(sol_t, t)
        push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
        push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
    end

    sol = FSPSolution{E}(sol_t, sol_snaps, sol_sizes, n_species)
    diag = KrylovFSPDiagnostics(τ_log, mass_log, time_log, walltime_log, size_log, reject_count, iter)

    (sol, diag)
end

# Krylov-FSP-SSA vs AdaptiveFSP Comparison
# For reviewer response: demonstrates flux-aware pruning advantages
#
# Tier 1: Oregonator — full quantitative comparison
# Tier 2: Bottleneck — connectivity failure diagnostic
# Tier 3: Robertson — stiffness failure diagnostic

using DiscStochSim, Catalyst, Random, Printf
using Plots

gr()
default(
    fontfamily="Computer Modern",
    titlefontsize=14,
    guidefontsize=12,
    tickfontsize=10,
    legendfontsize=9,
    linewidth=2,
    framestyle=:box,
    grid=false,
    dpi=300,
)

const OUTDIR = joinpath(@__DIR__, "output", "comparison")
mkpath(OUTDIR)

# ============================================================================
# Tier 1: Oregonator — Full Quantitative Comparison
# ============================================================================
function run_oregonator_comparison()
    println("=" ^ 60)
    println("TIER 1: Oregonator — Full Quantitative Comparison")
    println("=" ^ 60)

    rn = @reaction_network begin
        @species X(t) Y(t) Z(t)
        @parameters k1 k2 k3 k4 k5
        k1, Y --> X
        k2, X + Y --> 0
        k3, X --> 2X + Z
        k4, 2X --> 0
        k5, Z --> Y
    end

    y1s, y2s, y3s = 500.0, 1000.0, 2000.0
    mu1s, mu2s = 2000.0, 50000.0
    rates = [
        mu1s / y2s,
        mu2s / (y1s * y2s),
        (mu1s + mu2s) / y1s,
        2 * mu1s / y1s^2,
        (mu1s + mu2s) / y3s,
    ]

    tfinal = 0.11
    prob = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(500, 1000, 2000), (0.0, tfinal), rates;
                      bounds=(0, 50_000))

    # Run AdaptiveFSP
    println("\nRunning AdaptiveFSP...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_afsp_start = time()
    sol_afsp = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(

function run_bottleneck_comparison()
    println("\n" * "=" ^ 60)
    println("TIER 2: Bottleneck — Connectivity Failure Diagnostic")
    println("=" ^ 60)

    rn = @reaction_network begin
        k1, A --> B
        k2, B --> B + C
    end

    rates = [1e-6, 1e-1]
    bounds = (0, Int(1e11))
    prob = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(1, 0, 0), (0.0, 1e5), rates; bounds=bounds)

    # Run AdaptiveFSP (full, as reference)
    println("\nRunning AdaptiveFSP (reference)...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_afsp_start = time()
    sol_afsp = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(
        ε_dt=1.0, prob_quantile=0.9, flux_tolerance=1e-6, save_interval=1000,
    ))
    t_afsp = time() - t_afsp_start
    traj_afsp = mean_trajectory(sol_afsp)
    println("  AdaptiveFSP: $(length(sol_afsp)) snapshots, $(round(t_afsp; digits=1))s")

    # Run KrylovFSP (capped iterations — diagnostic)
    println("\nRunning KrylovFSP (max_iter=500, diagnostic)...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_kfsp_start = time()
    sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp = solve(prob, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-4, τ_init=1e3, ℓ=5, r=1, save_interval=100, max_iter=500,
    ))
    t_kfsp = time() - t_kfsp_start
    traj_kfsp = mean_trajectory(sol_kfsp)
    println("  KrylovFSP: $(diag_kfsp.total_iters) iters, $(diag_kfsp.reject_count) rejections")

    # Check if B=1 state was lost in KrylovFSP
    bottleneck_state = CartesianIndex(0, 1, 0)
    if length(sol_kfsp) > 0
        final_states_kfsp = sol_kfsp.snapshots[end][1]
        has_bottleneck = any(s -> s[2] >= 1, final_states_kfsp)
        println("  KrylovFSP has B>=1 state at end: $has_bottleneck")
    end

    # Check bottleneck presence in AdaptiveFSP
    if length(sol_afsp) > 0
        final_states_afsp = sol_afsp.snapshots[end][1]
        has_bottleneck_afsp = any(s -> s[2] >= 1, final_states_afsp)
        println("  AdaptiveFSP has B>=1 state at end: $has_bottleneck_afsp")
    end

    # Print results table
    println("\n--- Bottleneck Results ---")
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15s  %15s", "", "AdaptiveFSP", "KrylovFSP"))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.2f  %15.2f", "Wall time (s)", t_afsp, t_kfsp))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15d  %15d", "Snapshots", length(sol_afsp), length(sol_kfsp)))
    t_reached_afsp = sol_afsp.t[end]
    t_reached_kfsp = sol_kfsp.t[end]
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.2e  %15.2e", "Time reached", t_reached_afsp, t_reached_kfsp))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.4f  %15.4f", "Final <A>", traj_afsp[end, 1], traj_kfsp[end, 1]))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.4f  %15.4f", "Final <B>", traj_afsp[end, 2], traj_kfsp[end, 2]))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.4f  %15.4f", "Final <C>", traj_afsp[end, 3], traj_kfsp[end, 3]))

    # Generate plots
    # (a) Mean of C over time
    p1 = plot(title="(a) Mean C trajectory", xlabel="Time", ylabel="<C>")
    plot!(p1, sol_afsp.t, traj_afsp[:, 3], label="AdaptiveFSP", color=:blue, linewidth=2)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p1, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 3], label="KrylovFSP", color=:red,
              linestyle=:dash, linewidth=2)
    end

    # (b) Mean of B over time (shows bottleneck loss)
    p2 = plot(title="(b) Mean B trajectory", xlabel="Time", ylabel="<B>")
    plot!(p2, sol_afsp.t, traj_afsp[:, 2], label="AdaptiveFSP", color=:blue, linewidth=2)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p2, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 2], label="KrylovFSP", color=:red,
              linestyle=:dash, linewidth=2)
    end

    # (c) State space size
    p3 = plot(title="(c) State space size", xlabel="Time", ylabel="|S|")
    plot!(p3, sol_afsp.t, sol_afsp.state_space_sizes, label="AdaptiveFSP", color=:blue)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p3, sol_kfsp.t, sol_kfsp.state_space_sizes, label="KrylovFSP", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    # (d) KrylovFSP diagnostics: τ and mass over iterations
    p4 = plot(title="(d) KrylovFSP diagnostics", xlabel="Iteration", ylabel="Value")
    if length(diag_kfsp.τ_log) > 0
        iters = 1:length(diag_kfsp.τ_log)
        plot!(p4, iters, diag_kfsp.τ_log, label="τ", color=:blue, yscale=:log10)
        plot!(twinx(p4), iters, diag_kfsp.mass_log, label="mass", color=:red,
              linestyle=:dash, ylabel="Mass", legend=:bottomright)
    end

    fig = plot(p1, p2, p3, p4; layout=(2, 2), size=(1200, 800), margin=5Plots.mm)
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "bottleneck_comparison.png"))
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "bottleneck_comparison.pdf"))
    println("Saved bottleneck_comparison.{png,pdf}")

    return (sol_afsp=sol_afsp, sol_kfsp=sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp=diag_kfsp)
end

# Tier 3: Robertson — Stiffness Failure Diagnostic
# ============================================================================
function run_robertson_comparison()
    println("\n" * "=" ^ 60)
    println("TIER 3: Robertson — Stiffness Failure Diagnostic")
    println("=" ^ 60)

    rn = @reaction_network begin
        k1, A --> B
        k2, 2B --> C + B
        k3, C + B --> A + C
    end

    rates = [0.04, 3e6, 1.0]
    bounds = (0, 100_001)
    prob = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(10_000, 0, 0), (0.0, 1e4), rates;
                      bounds=bounds)

    # Run AdaptiveFSP
    println("\nRunning AdaptiveFSP...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_afsp_start = time()
    sol_afsp = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(
        ε_dt=0.01, prob_quantile=0.4, flux_tolerance=1e-9, save_interval=1000,
    ))
    t_afsp = time() - t_afsp_start
    traj_afsp = mean_trajectory(sol_afsp)
    println("  AdaptiveFSP: $(length(sol_afsp)) snapshots, $(round(t_afsp; digits=1))s")

    # Run KrylovFSP (capped — diagnostic)
    println("\nRunning KrylovFSP (max_iter=200, diagnostic)...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_kfsp_start = time()
    sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp = solve(prob, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-4, τ_init=0.1, ℓ=5, r=1, save_interval=50, max_iter=200,
    ))
    t_kfsp = time() - t_kfsp_start
    traj_kfsp = mean_trajectory(sol_kfsp)
    println("  KrylovFSP: $(diag_kfsp.total_iters) iters, $(diag_kfsp.reject_count) rejections")

    # Compute extrapolated completion time
    t_reached = sol_kfsp.t[end]
    tf = 1e4
    if t_reached > 0 && t_kfsp > 0
        extrapolated = t_kfsp * (tf / t_reached)
    else
        extrapolated = Inf
    end

    # Print results table
    println("\n--- Robertson Results ---")
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15s  %15s", "", "AdaptiveFSP", "KrylovFSP"))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.2f  %15.2f", "Wall time (s)", t_afsp, t_kfsp))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15d  %15d", "Total iterations", length(sol_afsp.t)-1, diag_kfsp.total_iters))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.2e  %15.2e", "Time reached", sol_afsp.t[end], t_reached))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15s  %15d", "Rejections", "N/A", diag_kfsp.reject_count))
    if length(diag_kfsp.τ_log) > 0
        println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15s  %15.2e", "Final τ", "N/A", diag_kfsp.τ_log[end]))
    end
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15s  %15.2e", "Extrapolated completion (s)", "---", extrapolated))

    # Generate plots
    # (a) τ vs iteration (shows halving cascade)
    p1 = plot(title="(a) τ vs iteration", xlabel="Iteration", ylabel="τ", yscale=:log10)
    if length(diag_kfsp.τ_log) > 0
        plot!(p1, 1:length(diag_kfsp.τ_log), diag_kfsp.τ_log,
              label="KrylovFSP τ", color=:red, linewidth=2)
    end

    # (b) Simulated time reached vs wall time
    p2 = plot(title="(b) Simulated time vs wall time",
              xlabel="Wall time (s)", ylabel="Simulated time")
    if length(diag_kfsp.walltime_log) > 0
        plot!(p2, diag_kfsp.walltime_log, diag_kfsp.time_log,
              label="KrylovFSP", color=:red, linewidth=2)
    end
    # Show AdaptiveFSP final point for reference
    scatter!(p2, [t_afsp], [sol_afsp.t[end]], label="AdaptiveFSP (complete)",
             color=:blue, markersize=8, markershape=:star5)

    # (c) Mass conservation over iterations
    p3 = plot(title="(c) Probability mass", xlabel="Iteration", ylabel="Mass")
    if length(diag_kfsp.mass_log) > 0
        plot!(p3, 1:length(diag_kfsp.mass_log), diag_kfsp.mass_log,
              label="KrylovFSP mass", color=:red, linewidth=2)
    end

    # (d) State space size over iterations
    p4 = plot(title="(d) State space size", xlabel="Iteration", ylabel="|S|")
    if length(diag_kfsp.size_log) > 0
        plot!(p4, 1:length(diag_kfsp.size_log), diag_kfsp.size_log,
              label="KrylovFSP", color=:red, linewidth=2)
    end

    fig = plot(p1, p2, p3, p4; layout=(2, 2), size=(1200, 800), margin=5Plots.mm)
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "robertson_comparison.png"))
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "robertson_comparison.pdf"))
    println("Saved robertson_comparison.{png,pdf}")

    return (sol_afsp=sol_afsp, sol_kfsp=sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp=diag_kfsp)
end

"""
    KrylovFSP(; kwargs...)

Krylov-FSP-SSA baseline algorithm (Sidje & Vo 2015, reviewed in Dinh & Sidje 2016).

Uses probability-threshold pruning (no flux protection), mass-conservation
accept/reject time stepping, and SSA-driven + reachability expansion.

# Keyword Arguments
- `ε::Float64 = 1e-3`: Total probability mass loss tolerance.
- `τ_init::Float64 = 1.0`: Initial time step.
- `prob_threshold::Float64 = 0.0`: Hard probability threshold for pruning (0 = use ε/|S|).
- `ℓ::Int = 5`: Lookback window length for max-probability tracking.
- `r::Int = 1`: Reachability expansion depth after SSA.
- `save_interval::Int = 1000`: Save a snapshot every N iterations.
- `max_iter::Int = typemax(Int)`: Maximum number of iterations (for diagnostic runs).
"""
Base.@kwdef struct KrylovFSP
    ε::Float64 = 1e-3
    τ_init::Float64 = 1.0
    prob_threshold::Float64 = 0.0
    ℓ::Int = 5
    r::Int = 1
    save_interval::Int = 1000
    max_iter::Int = typemax(Int)
end

"""
    KrylovFSPDiagnostics

Per-iteration diagnostic data from a KrylovFSP solve.
"""
struct KrylovFSPDiagnostics
    τ_log::Vector{Float64}
    mass_log::Vector{Float64}
    time_log::Vector{Float64}
    walltime_log::Vector{Float64}
    size_log::Vector{Int}
    reject_count::Int
    total_iters::Int
end

"""
    solve(prob::FSPProblem, alg::KrylovFSP) -> (FSPSolution, KrylovFSPDiagnostics)

Run the Krylov-FSP-SSA algorithm (Dinh & Sidje 2016, Algorithm [18]).

Returns a tuple of `(solution, diagnostics)` where diagnostics contains
per-iteration τ, mass, timing, and rejection data for failure-mode analysis.
"""
function CommonSolve.solve(prob::FSPProblem{E,T}, alg::KrylovFSP) where {E,T}
    model = prob.model
    rates = prob.rates
    bc = prob.bc
    t0, tf = prob.tspan
    n_species = length(Tuple(prob.u0))

    # Initialize state space
    sp = StateSpace{E, Float64}()
    add_state!(sp, prob.u0, 1.0)

    # Solution storage
    sol_t = Float64[t0]
    sol_snaps = [(copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs))]
    sol_sizes = [length(sp)]

    # Diagnostics
    τ_log = Float64[]
    mass_log = Float64[]
    time_log = Float64[]
    walltime_log = Float64[]
    size_log = Int[]
    reject_count = 0

    # Lookback window for max-probability tracking
    prob_history = Vector{Dict{E,Float64}}()

    t = Float64(t0)
    τ = Float64(alg.τ_init)
    iter = 0
    wall_start = time()

    while t < tf && iter < alg.max_iter
        iter += 1

        # Determine pruning threshold
        threshold = alg.prob_threshold > 0 ? alg.prob_threshold : alg.ε / max(length(sp), 1)

        # Update lookback window
        current_probs = Dict{E,Float64}(s => sp.probs[sp.index[s]] for s in sp.states)
        push!(prob_history, current_probs)
        if length(prob_history) > alg.ℓ
            popfirst!(prob_history)
        end

        # Compute max probability over lookback window
        max_probs = Dict{E,Float64}()
        for hist in prob_history
            for (s, p) in hist
                max_probs[s] = max(get(max_probs, s, 0.0), p)
            end
        end

        # 1. Threshold prune (with lookback protection)
        prune_threshold!(sp, threshold; max_probs=max_probs)

        # 2. SSA-driven expansion
        expand_ssa!(sp, model, rates, t, bc; depth=1)

        # 3. r-step reachability expansion
        if alg.r > 0
            expand!(sp, model, bc; depth=alg.r)
        end

        # 4. Build generator + propagate
        τ_step = min(τ, tf - t)
        A, _, _ = build_generator(sp, model, rates, t)
        p_new = expmv(τ_step, A, sp.probs)

        # 5. Accept/reject based on mass conservation
        mass = sum(p_new)
        mass_target = 1.0 - alg.ε * (t + τ_step) / tf

        if mass >= mass_target
            # Accept step
            sp.probs = p_new
            t += τ_step

            push!(τ_log, τ_step)
            push!(mass_log, mass)
            push!(time_log, t)
            push!(walltime_log, time() - wall_start)
            push!(size_log, length(sp))

            # Save snapshot
            if iter % alg.save_interval == 0 || t >= tf
                push!(sol_t, t)
                push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
                push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
                @info "KrylovFSP: t = $(round(t; sigdigits=4)), |S| = $(length(sp)), τ = $(round(τ_step; sigdigits=3)), mass = $(round(mass; sigdigits=6))"
            end
        else
            # Reject: halve τ
            τ /= 2
            reject_count += 1

            push!(τ_log, τ_step)
            push!(mass_log, mass)
            push!(time_log, t)
            push!(walltime_log, time() - wall_start)
            push!(size_log, length(sp))

            if iter % alg.save_interval == 0
                @info "KrylovFSP REJECT: t = $(round(t; sigdigits=4)), τ = $(round(τ; sigdigits=3)), mass = $(round(mass; sigdigits=6))"
            end
        end
    end

    # Ensure final snapshot is captured (avoid duplicate if already saved in loop)
    if length(sol_t) == 1 || sol_t[end] < t - eps(t)
        push!(sol_t, t)
        push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
        push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
    end

    sol = FSPSolution{E}(sol_t, sol_snaps, sol_sizes, n_species)
    diag = KrylovFSPDiagnostics(τ_log, mass_log, time_log, walltime_log, size_log, reject_count, iter)

    (sol, diag)
end

So the problem is clear: KrylovFSP rejects almost every step because the mass conservation criterion is too tight for the Oregonator. With τ_init=1e-5 the initial steps pass but τ gets halved to effectively 0 and makes no progress. This is actually the exact diagnostic result we want for the paper — the accept/reject stepping fails on stiff oscillatory systems.

However, for the Oregonator we want to show it *can* complete (both methods should work on this system per the plan). Let me use a more generous ε and a reasonable τ:

The issue is that the mass conservation criterion is being applied too strictly. Let me look at it more carefully.

The mass target is: `1.0 - alg.ε * (t + τ_step) / tf`

At t=0, τ_step=1e-6, tf=0.11:
mass_target = 1.0 - 0.1 * (0 + 1e-6) / 0.11 = 1.0 - 9.09e-7 ≈ 0.9999991

But mass after first step = 0.990408, which is way below. The problem is that the expansion adds many states and the probability leaks significantly even in one step, because the state space is very large and the pruning is too aggressive with the threshold.


Actually, I see the real problem now — the criterion `1.0 - ε * (t+τ)/tf` is essentially requiring near-perfect conservation at t≈0, but with propensities around 50000 in the Oregonator, even tiny steps lose mass to boundary states. The KrylovFSP method needs a much larger initial state space to handle this system effectively.

This actually strengthens the paper's narrative. If KrylovFSP struggles on the Oregonator too, that demonstrates the flux-adaptive method's superiority even on a "normal" system, not just on the pathological cases. I could cap the KrylovFSP run and present it as a diagnostic showing how the accept/reject stepping fails across all three scenarios.

Now I'm realizing the issue with the accept/reject criterion itself — at t≈0, it's essentially requiring mass ≥ 1.0, which is far too strict. The budget should scale with time advancement, so early steps get proportionally smaller allowances. With the numbers I'm checking, even a 1% loss in the first step exceeds what the criterion permits, which explains why KrylovFSP is failing so badly.

The real bottleneck though is that the state space is too sparse. Starting from a single state and expanding only to immediate neighbors gives maybe 100 states, but the propensities are huge — around 50,000 — so most of the probability flow escapes to boundary states that aren't even in the active set. The reference algorithm would start with a much larger pre-expanded state space, not just r=1 neighbors. I should try increasing the expansion depth to r=2 or r=3, or be more aggressive about the initial state space size.

But stepping back, maybe the real issue is that KrylovFSP with such a tiny τ_init=1e-6 is fundamentally incompatible with how sparse the initial state space is. The AdaptiveFSP uses a much smaller dt≈6e-6 and still works because it's designed differently. Once the SSA expansion happens with r=1, the state space is just too limited to handle the dynamics properly. reachability, we get maybe 10-20 states. Then `build_generator` is called, and the matrix exponential pushes probability to boundary states (which aren't in our set), so mass drops. With only a few states, mass loss is huge.

Compare to AdaptiveFSP: it also starts from 1 state but its first dt is `ε_dt / total_flux = 1.0 / (huge propensity) ≈ tiny`. So AdaptiveFSP's first step is incredibly tiny, and then the state space grows quickly.

For KrylovFSP, the issue is that τ_init=1e-6 is already too large for the initial tiny state space. After many rejections and halvings, τ→0 and no progress is made.

The real algorithm uses multiple SSA expansion rounds to build up the state space before attempting propagation, but I'm jumping straight to propagation with too few states. I think the best approach is to pre-expand aggressively with higher reachability depth before starting the main loop, rather than trying to make the initial propagation work with a minimal state space.

# Krylov-FSP-SSA vs AdaptiveFSP Comparison
# For reviewer response: demonstrates flux-aware pruning advantages
#
# Tier 1: Oregonator — full quantitative comparison
# Tier 2: Bottleneck — connectivity failure diagnostic
# Tier 3: Robertson — stiffness failure diagnostic

using DiscStochSim, Catalyst, Random, Printf
using Plots

gr()
default(
    fontfamily="Computer Modern",
    titlefontsize=14,
    guidefontsize=12,
    tickfontsize=10,
    legendfontsize=9,
    linewidth=2,
    framestyle=:box,
    grid=false,
    dpi=300,
)

const OUTDIR = joinpath(@__DIR__, "output", "comparison")
mkpath(OUTDIR)

# ============================================================================
# Tier 1: Oregonator — Full Quantitative Comparison
# ============================================================================
function run_oregonator_comparison()
    println("=" ^ 60)
    println("TIER 1: Oregonator — Full Quantitative Comparison")
    println("=" ^ 60)

    rn = @reaction_network begin
        @species X(t) Y(t) Z(t)
        @parameters k1 k2 k3 k4 k5
        k1, Y --> X
        k2, X + Y --> 0
        k3, X --> 2X + Z
        k4, 2X --> 0
        k5, Z --> Y
    end

    y1s, y2s, y3s = 500.0, 1000.0, 2000.0
    mu1s, mu2s = 2000.0, 50000.0
    rates = [
        mu1s / y2s,
        mu2s / (y1s * y2s),
        (mu1s + mu2s) / y1s,
        2 * mu1s / y1s^2,
        (mu1s + mu2s) / y3s,
    ]

    tfinal = 0.11
    prob = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(500, 1000, 2000), (0.0, tfinal), rates;
                      bounds=(0, 50_000))

    # Run AdaptiveFSP
    println("\nRunning AdaptiveFSP...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_afsp_start = time()
    sol_afsp = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(
        ε_dt=1.0, prob_quantile=0.1, flux_tolerance=1.0,
        expansion_depth=1, save_interval=1000,
    ))
    t_afsp = time() - t_afsp_start
    traj_afsp = mean_trajectory(sol_afsp)

    # Run KrylovFSP
    # τ_init=1e-5 matches the natural time scale (AdaptiveFSP dt ≈ 6e-6)
    # max_iter=30000 caps runtime for feasibility
    println("\nRunning KrylovFSP...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_kfsp_start = time()
    sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp = solve(prob, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-3, τ_init=1e-5, ℓ=5, r=1, save_interval=1000, max_iter=30000,
    ))
    t_kfsp = time() - t_kfsp_start
    traj_kfsp = mean_trajectory(sol_kfsp)

    # Print results table
    println("\n--- Oregonator Results ---")
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15s  %15s", "", "AdaptiveFSP", "KrylovFSP"))
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15.2f  %15.2f", "Wall time (s)", t_afsp, t_kfsp))
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15d  %15d", "Snapshots", length(sol_afsp), length(sol_kfsp)))
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15d  %15d", "Final |S|",
            sol_afsp.state_space_sizes[end], sol_kfsp.state_space_sizes[end]))
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15d  %15d", "Max |S|",
            maximum(sol_afsp.state_space_sizes), maximum(sol_kfsp.state_space_sizes)))
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15d", "KrylovFSP rejections", diag_kfsp.reject_count))
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15d", "KrylovFSP total iters", diag_kfsp.total_iters))

    # Generate plots
    # (a) Mean trajectories overlaid
    p1 = plot(title="(a) Mean trajectories", xlabel="Time", ylabel="Population")
    plot!(p1, sol_afsp.t, traj_afsp[:, 1], label="X (AdaptiveFSP)", color=:blue, linestyle=:solid)
    plot!(p1, sol_afsp.t, traj_afsp[:, 2], label="Y (AdaptiveFSP)", color=:red, linestyle=:solid)
    plot!(p1, sol_afsp.t, traj_afsp[:, 3], label="Z (AdaptiveFSP)", color=:green, linestyle=:solid)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p1, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 1], label="X (KrylovFSP)", color=:blue, linestyle=:dash)
        plot!(p1, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 2], label="Y (KrylovFSP)", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
        plot!(p1, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 3], label="Z (KrylovFSP)", color=:green, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    # (b) State space size over time
    p2 = plot(title="(b) State space size", xlabel="Time", ylabel="|S|")
    plot!(p2, sol_afsp.t, sol_afsp.state_space_sizes, label="AdaptiveFSP", color=:blue)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p2, sol_kfsp.t, sol_kfsp.state_space_sizes, label="KrylovFSP", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    # (c) dt/τ over time
    p3 = plot(title="(c) Time step size", xlabel="Time", ylabel="dt / τ", yscale=:log10)
    if length(sol_afsp.t) > 1
        dt_afsp = diff(sol_afsp.t)
        plot!(p3, sol_afsp.t[2:end], dt_afsp, label="AdaptiveFSP dt", color=:blue)
    end
    if length(diag_kfsp.τ_log) > 0
        plot!(p3, diag_kfsp.time_log, diag_kfsp.τ_log, label="KrylovFSP τ", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    # (d) Marginal distribution at final time
    p4 = plot(title="(d) Marginal P(X) at t_f", xlabel="X", ylabel="Probability")
    if length(sol_afsp) > 0
        m_afsp = marginal(sol_afsp, length(sol_afsp), 1)
        bar!(p4, m_afsp.values, m_afsp.probs, label="AdaptiveFSP", alpha=0.5, color=:blue)
    end
    if length(sol_kfsp) > 0
        m_kfsp = marginal(sol_kfsp, length(sol_kfsp), 1)
        bar!(p4, m_kfsp.values, m_kfsp.probs, label="KrylovFSP", alpha=0.5, color=:red)
    end

    fig = plot(p1, p2, p3, p4; layout=(2, 2), size=(1200, 800), margin=5Plots.mm)
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "oregonator_comparison.png"))
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "oregonator_comparison.pdf"))
    println("Saved oregonator_comparison.{png,pdf}")

    return (sol_afsp=sol_afsp, sol_kfsp=sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp=diag_kfsp,
            t_afsp=t_afsp, t_kfsp=t_kfsp)
end

# ============================================================================
# Tier 2: Bottleneck — Connectivity Failure Diagnostic
# ============================================================================
function run_bottleneck_comparison()
    println("\n" * "=" ^ 60)
    println("TIER 2: Bottleneck — Connectivity Failure Diagnostic")
    println("=" ^ 60)

    rn = @reaction_network begin
        k1, A --> B
        k2, B --> B + C
    end

    rates = [1e-6, 1e-1]
    bounds = (0, Int(1e11))
    prob = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(1, 0, 0), (0.0, 1e5), rates; bounds=bounds)

    # Run AdaptiveFSP (full, as reference)
    println("\nRunning AdaptiveFSP (reference)...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_afsp_start = time()
    sol_afsp = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(
        ε_dt=1.0, prob_quantile=0.9, flux_tolerance=1e-6, save_interval=1000,
    ))
    t_afsp = time() - t_afsp_start
    traj_afsp = mean_trajectory(sol_afsp)
    println("  AdaptiveFSP: $(length(sol_afsp)) snapshots, $(round(t_afsp; digits=1))s")

    # Run KrylovFSP (capped iterations — diagnostic)
    println("\nRunning KrylovFSP (max_iter=500, diagnostic)...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_kfsp_start = time()
    sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp = solve(prob, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-4, τ_init=1e3, ℓ=5, r=1, save_interval=100, max_iter=500,
    ))
    t_kfsp = time() - t_kfsp_start
    traj_kfsp = mean_trajectory(sol_kfsp)
    println("  KrylovFSP: $(diag_kfsp.total_iters) iters, $(diag_kfsp.reject_count) rejections")

    # Check if B=1 state was lost in KrylovFSP
    bottleneck_state = CartesianIndex(0, 1, 0)
    if length(sol_kfsp) > 0
        final_states_kfsp = sol_kfsp.snapshots[end][1]
        has_bottleneck = any(s -> s[2] >= 1, final_states_kfsp)
        println("  KrylovFSP has B>=1 state at end: $has_bottleneck")
    end

    # Check bottleneck presence in AdaptiveFSP
    if length(sol_afsp) > 0
        final_states_afsp = sol_afsp.snapshots[end][1]
        has_bottleneck_afsp = any(s -> s[2] >= 1, final_states_afsp)
        println("  AdaptiveFSP has B>=1 state at end: $has_bottleneck_afsp")
    end

    # Print results table
    println("\n--- Bottleneck Results ---")
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15s  %15s", "", "AdaptiveFSP", "KrylovFSP"))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.2f  %15.2f", "Wall time (s)", t_afsp, t_kfsp))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15d  %15d", "Snapshots", length(sol_afsp), length(sol_kfsp)))
    t_reached_afsp = sol_afsp.t[end]
    t_reached_kfsp = sol_kfsp.t[end]
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.2e  %15.2e", "Time reached", t_reached_afsp, t_reached_kfsp))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.4f  %15.4f", "Final <A>", traj_afsp[end, 1], traj_kfsp[end, 1]))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.4f  %15.4f", "Final <B>", traj_afsp[end, 2], traj_kfsp[end, 2]))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.4f  %15.4f", "Final <C>", traj_afsp[end, 3], traj_kfsp[end, 3]))

    # Generate plots
    # (a) Mean of C over time
    p1 = plot(title="(a) Mean C trajectory", xlabel="Time", ylabel="<C>")
    plot!(p1, sol_afsp.t, traj_afsp[:, 3], label="AdaptiveFSP", color=:blue, linewidth=2)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p1, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 3], label="KrylovFSP", color=:red,
              linestyle=:dash, linewidth=2)
    end

    # (b) Mean of B over time (shows bottleneck loss)
    p2 = plot(title="(b) Mean B trajectory", xlabel="Time", ylabel="<B>")

    end

    # (c) State space size
    p3 = plot(title="(c) State space size", xlabel="Time", ylabel="|S|")
    plot!(p3, sol_afsp.t, sol_afsp.state_space_sizes, label="AdaptiveFSP", color=:blue)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p3, sol_kfsp.t, sol_kfsp.state_space_sizes, label="KrylovFSP", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    # (d) KrylovFSP diagnostics: τ and mass over iterations
    p4 = plot(title="(d) KrylovFSP diagnostics", xlabel="Iteration", ylabel="Value")
    if length(diag_kfsp.τ_log) > 0
        iters = 1:length(diag_kfsp.τ_log)
        plot!(p4, iters, diag_kfsp.τ_log, label="τ", color=:blue, yscale=:log10)
        plot!(twinx(p4), iters, diag_kfsp.mass_log, label="mass", color=:red,

function run_robertson_comparison()
    println("\n" * "=" ^ 60)
    println("TIER 3: Robertson — Stiffness Failure Diagnostic")
    println("=" ^ 60)

    rn = @reaction_network begin
        k1, A --> B
        k2, 2B --> C + B
        k3, C + B --> A + C
    end

    rates = [0.04, 3e6, 1.0]
    bounds = (0, 100_001)
    prob = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(10_000, 0, 0), (0.0, 1e4), rates;
                      bounds=bounds)

    # Run AdaptiveFSP
    println("\nRunning AdaptiveFSP...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_afsp_start = time()
    sol_afsp = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(
        ε_dt=0.01, prob_quantile=0.4, flux_tolerance=1e-9, save_interval=1000,
    ))
    t_afsp = time() - t_afsp_start
    traj_afsp = mean_trajectory(sol_afsp)
    println("  AdaptiveFSP: $(length(sol_afsp)) snapshots, $(round(t_afsp; digits=1))s")

    # Run KrylovFSP (capped — diagnostic)
    println("\nRunning KrylovFSP (max_iter=200, diagnostic)...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_kfsp_start = time()
    sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp = solve(prob, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-4, τ_init=0.1, ℓ=5, r=1, save_interval=50, max_iter=200,
    ))
    t_kfsp = time() - t_kfsp_start
    traj_kfsp = mean_trajectory(sol_kfsp)
    println("  KrylovFSP: $(diag_kfsp.total_iters) iters, $(diag_kfsp.reject_count) rejections")

    # Compute extrapolated completion time
    t_reached = sol_kfsp.t[end]
    tf = 1e4
    if t_reached > 0 && t_kfsp > 0
        extrapolated = t_kfsp * (tf / t_reached)
    else
        extrapolated = Inf
    end

    # Print results table
    println("\n--- Robertson Results ---")
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15s  %15s", "", "AdaptiveFSP", "KrylovFSP"))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.2f  %15.2f", "Wall time (s)", t_afsp, t_kfsp))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15d  %15d", "Total iterations", length(sol_afsp.t)-1, diag_kfsp.total_iters))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.2e  %15.2e", "Time reached", sol_afsp.t[end], t_reached))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15s  %15d", "Rejections", "N/A", diag_kfsp.reject_count))
    if length(diag_kfsp.τ_log) > 0
        println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15s  %15.2e", "Final τ", "N/A", diag_kfsp.τ_log[end]))
    end
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15s  %15.2e", "Extrapolated completion (s)", "---", extrapolated))

    # Generate plots
    # (a) τ vs iteration (shows halving cascade)
    p1 = plot(title="(a) τ vs iteration", xlabel="Iteration", ylabel="τ", yscale=:log10)
    if length(diag_kfsp.τ_log) > 0
        plot!(p1, 1:length(diag_kfsp.τ_log), diag_kfsp.τ_log,
              label="KrylovFSP τ", color=:red, linewidth=2)
    end

    # (b) Simulated time reached vs wall time
    p2 = plot(title="(b) Simulated time vs wall time",
              xlabel="Wall time (s)", ylabel="Simulated time")
    if length(diag_kfsp.walltime_log) > 0
        plot!(p2, diag_kfsp.walltime_log, diag_kfsp.time_log,
              label="KrylovFSP", color=:red, linewidth=2)
    end
    # Show AdaptiveFSP final point for reference
    scatter!(p2, [t_afsp], [sol_afsp.t[end]], label="AdaptiveFSP (complete)",
             color=:blue, markersize=8, markershape=:star5)

    # (c) Mass conservation over iterations
    p3 = plot(title="(c) Probability mass", xlabel="Iteration", ylabel="Mass")
    if length(diag_kfsp.mass_log) > 0
        plot!(p3, 1:length(diag_kfsp.mass_log), diag_kfsp.mass_log,
              label="KrylovFSP mass", color=:red, linewidth=2)
    end

    # (d) State space size over iterations
    p4 = plot(title="(d) State space size", xlabel="Iteration", ylabel="|S|")
    if length(diag_kfsp.size_log) > 0
        plot!(p4, 1:length(diag_kfsp.size_log), diag_kfsp.size_log,
              label="KrylovFSP", color=:red, linewidth=2)
    end

    fig = plot(p1, p2, p3, p4; layout=(2, 2), size=(1200, 800), margin=5Plots.mm)
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "robertson_comparison.png"))
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "robertson_comparison.pdf"))
    println("Saved robertson_comparison.{png,pdf}")

    return (sol_afsp=sol_afsp, sol_kfsp=sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp=diag_kfsp)
end

Even with r=3 and larger state space (74-325 states), the mass conservation criterion is too strict. The issue: at the start when t is very small, mass_target ≈ 1.0 - ε * tiny/tf ≈ 1.0, so virtually no mass loss is tolerated. But even with 325 states, the Oregonator's huge propensities push probability to boundary states.

Looking at the mass: 0.999013. The target is 1.0 - 0.01 * 1e-6/0.11 = 0.99999999. 

I think the problem is that I'm using a time-proportional budget formula when the original algorithm just uses a fixed tolerance. Let me check what the Dinh & Sidje algorithm actually specifies for the acceptance criterion—it should be something like checking if the total probability loss stays within a constant bound, not one that shrinks as time progresses. I'm switching to the standard acceptance criterion from the literature: the sum of probabilities must stay above `1 - ε_tol`, where `ε_tol` is the total tolerance budget. This is cleaner than my cumulative time-based formula.

"""
    KrylovFSP(; kwargs...)

Krylov-FSP-SSA baseline algorithm (Sidje & Vo 2015, reviewed in Dinh & Sidje 2016).

Uses probability-threshold pruning (no flux protection), mass-conservation
accept/reject time stepping, and SSA-driven + reachability expansion.

# Keyword Arguments
- `ε::Float64 = 1e-3`: Total probability mass loss tolerance.
- `τ_init::Float64 = 1.0`: Initial time step.
- `prob_threshold::Float64 = 0.0`: Hard probability threshold for pruning (0 = use ε/|S|).
- `ℓ::Int = 5`: Lookback window length for max-probability tracking.
- `r::Int = 1`: Reachability expansion depth after SSA.
- `save_interval::Int = 1000`: Save a snapshot every N iterations.
- `max_iter::Int = typemax(Int)`: Maximum number of iterations (for diagnostic runs).
"""
Base.@kwdef struct KrylovFSP
    ε::Float64 = 1e-3
    τ_init::Float64 = 1.0
    prob_threshold::Float64 = 0.0
    ℓ::Int = 5
    r::Int = 1
    save_interval::Int = 1000
    max_iter::Int = typemax(Int)
end

"""
    KrylovFSPDiagnostics

Per-iteration diagnostic data from a KrylovFSP solve.
"""
struct KrylovFSPDiagnostics
    τ_log::Vector{Float64}
    mass_log::Vector{Float64}
    time_log::Vector{Float64}
    walltime_log::Vector{Float64}
    size_log::Vector{Int}
    reject_count::Int
    total_iters::Int
end

"""
    solve(prob::FSPProblem, alg::KrylovFSP) -> (FSPSolution, KrylovFSPDiagnostics)

Run the Krylov-FSP-SSA algorithm (Dinh & Sidje 2016, Algorithm [18]).

Returns a tuple of `(solution, diagnostics)` where diagnostics contains
per-iteration τ, mass, timing, and rejection data for failure-mode analysis.
"""
function CommonSolve.solve(prob::FSPProblem{E,T}, alg::KrylovFSP) where {E,T}
    model = prob.model
    rates = prob.rates
    bc = prob.bc
    t0, tf = prob.tspan
    n_species = length(Tuple(prob.u0))

    # Initialize state space
    sp = StateSpace{E, Float64}()
    add_state!(sp, prob.u0, 1.0)

    # Solution storage
    sol_t = Float64[t0]
    sol_snaps = [(copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs))]
    sol_sizes = [length(sp)]

    # Diagnostics
    τ_log = Float64[]
    mass_log = Float64[]
    time_log = Float64[]
    walltime_log = Float64[]
    size_log = Int[]
    reject_count = 0

    # Lookback window for max-probability tracking
    prob_history = Vector{Dict{E,Float64}}()

    t = Float64(t0)
    τ = Float64(alg.τ_init)
    iter = 0
    wall_start = time()

    while t < tf && iter < alg.max_iter
        iter += 1

        # Determine pruning threshold
        threshold = alg.prob_threshold > 0 ? alg.prob_threshold : alg.ε / max(length(sp), 1)

        # Update lookback window
        current_probs = Dict{E,Float64}(s => sp.probs[sp.index[s]] for s in sp.states)
        push!(prob_history, current_probs)
        if length(prob_history) > alg.ℓ
            popfirst!(prob_history)
        end

        # Compute max probability over lookback window
        max_probs = Dict{E,Float64}()
        for hist in prob_history
            for (s, p) in hist
                max_probs[s] = max(get(max_probs, s, 0.0), p)
            end
        end

        # 1. Threshold prune (with lookback protection)
        prune_threshold!(sp, threshold; max_probs=max_probs)

        # 2. SSA-driven expansion
        expand_ssa!(sp, model, rates, t, bc; depth=1)

        # 3. r-step reachability expansion
        if alg.r > 0
            expand!(sp, model, bc; depth=alg.r)
        end

        # 4. Build generator + propagate
        τ_step = min(τ, tf - t)
        A, _, _ = build_generator(sp, model, rates, t)

        # Attempt matrix exponential; if it fails numerically, reject and halve τ
        local p_new
        expmv_ok = true
        try
            p_new = expmv(τ_step, A, sp.probs)
            if any(isnan, p_new) || any(isinf, p_new)
                expmv_ok = false
            end
        catch
            expmv_ok = false
        end

        if !expmv_ok
            # Treat as rejection
            τ /= 2
            reject_count += 1
            push!(τ_log, τ_step)
            push!(mass_log, NaN)
            push!(time_log, t)
            push!(walltime_log, time() - wall_start)
            push!(size_log, length(sp))
            continue
        end

        # Clamp small negative values from numerical noise
        @inbounds for i in eachindex(p_new)
            if p_new[i] < 0
                p_new[i] = 0.0
            end
        end

        # 5. Accept/reject based on mass conservation
        mass = sum(p_new)
        mass_target = 1.0 - alg.ε * (t + τ_step) / tf

        if mass >= mass_target
            # Accept step
            sp.probs = p_new
            t += τ_step

            push!(τ_log, τ_step)
            push!(mass_log, mass)
            push!(time_log, t)
            push!(walltime_log, time() - wall_start)
            push!(size_log, length(sp))

            # Save snapshot
            if iter % alg.save_interval == 0 || t >= tf
                push!(sol_t, t)
                push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
                push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
                @info "KrylovFSP: t = $(round(t; sigdigits=4)), |S| = $(length(sp)), τ = $(round(τ_step; sigdigits=3)), mass = $(round(mass; sigdigits=6))"
            end
        else
            # Reject: halve τ
            τ /= 2
            reject_count += 1

            push!(τ_log, τ_step)
            push!(mass_log, mass)
            push!(time_log, t)
            push!(walltime_log, time() - wall_start)
            push!(size_log, length(sp))

            if iter % alg.save_interval == 0
                @info "KrylovFSP REJECT: t = $(round(t; sigdigits=4)), τ = $(round(τ; sigdigits=3)), mass = $(round(mass; sigdigits=6))"
            end
        end
    end

    # Ensure final snapshot is captured (avoid duplicate if already saved in loop)
    if length(sol_t) == 1 || sol_t[end] < t - eps(t)
        push!(sol_t, t)
        push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
        push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
    end

    sol = FSPSolution{E}(sol_t, sol_snaps, sol_sizes, n_species)
    diag = KrylovFSPDiagnostics(τ_log, mass_log, time_log, walltime_log, size_log, reject_count, iter)

    (sol, diag)
end

toolUseResult.originalFile:
using DiscStochSim, Catalyst, Random

rn = @reaction_network begin
    @species X(t) Y(t) Z(t)
    @parameters k1 k2 k3 k4 k5
    k1, Y --> X
    k2, X + Y --> 0
    k3, X --> 2X + Z
    k4, 2X --> 0
    k5, Z --> Y
end

y1s, y2s, y3s = 500.0, 1000.0, 2000.0
mu1s, mu2s = 2000.0, 50000.0
rates = [mu1s/y2s, mu2s/(y1s*y2s), (mu1s+mu2s)/y1s, 2*mu1s/y1s^2, (mu1s+mu2s)/y3s]
prob = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(500, 1000, 2000), (0.0, 0.11), rates; bounds=(0, 50_000))

Random.default_rng(1)
t0 = time()
sol, diag = solve(prob, KrylovFSP(ε=1e-2, τ_init=1e-6, ℓ=5, r=3, save_interval=5000, max_iter=5000))
elapsed = time() - t0

println("Iters: $(diag.total_iters), rejections: $(diag.reject_count)")
println("Time reached: $(sol.t[end]), wall: $(round(elapsed; digits=1))s")
println("Accepted: $(diag.total_iters - diag.reject_count)")
if length(diag.size_log) > 0
    println("|S| range: [$(minimum(diag.size_log)), $(maximum(diag.size_log))]")
end

content.thinking:
The problem is that at τ=0 (after many halvings), the mass is still ~0.95. That doesn't make sense unless expmv with τ=0 is returning something weird, or the issue is that the state space keeps changing between iterations.

Wait, the mass is 0.95 with τ ≈ 0 (after many halvings). That means p_new ≈ p_old (since τ≈0), so mass = sum(p_old) ≈ 0.95. The mass of the probability vector itself is less than 1 because of renormalization... wait, we don't renormalize in KrylovFSP.


Actually, I see the real issue now—mass isn't being preserved across steps. When we accept a step and update the probability vector, the new mass might be 0.96 instead of 1. Then the next iteration starts from that degraded state, and pruning removes more states, pushing mass even lower. The solution is to renormalize the probabilities after accepting each step so we always begin from mass=1, which is what the original Krylov-FSP algorithm does. I'll add that renormalization step after accepting.

"""
    KrylovFSP(; kwargs...)

Krylov-FSP-SSA baseline algorithm (Sidje & Vo 2015, reviewed in Dinh & Sidje 2016).

Uses probability-threshold pruning (no flux protection), mass-conservation
accept/reject time stepping, and SSA-driven + reachability expansion.

# Keyword Arguments
- `ε::Float64 = 1e-3`: Total probability mass loss tolerance.
- `τ_init::Float64 = 1.0`: Initial time step.
- `prob_threshold::Float64 = 0.0`: Hard probability threshold for pruning (0 = use ε/|S|).
- `ℓ::Int = 5`: Lookback window length for max-probability tracking.
- `r::Int = 1`: Reachability expansion depth after SSA.
- `save_interval::Int = 1000`: Save a snapshot every N iterations.
- `max_iter::Int = typemax(Int)`: Maximum number of iterations (for diagnostic runs).
"""
Base.@kwdef struct KrylovFSP
    ε::Float64 = 1e-3
    τ_init::Float64 = 1.0
    prob_threshold::Float64 = 0.0
    ℓ::Int = 5
    r::Int = 1
    save_interval::Int = 1000
    max_iter::Int = typemax(Int)
end

"""
    KrylovFSPDiagnostics

Per-iteration diagnostic data from a KrylovFSP solve.
"""
struct KrylovFSPDiagnostics
    τ_log::Vector{Float64}
    mass_log::Vector{Float64}
    time_log::Vector{Float64}
    walltime_log::Vector{Float64}
    size_log::Vector{Int}
    reject_count::Int
    total_iters::Int
end

"""
    solve(prob::FSPProblem, alg::KrylovFSP) -> (FSPSolution, KrylovFSPDiagnostics)

Run the Krylov-FSP-SSA algorithm (Dinh & Sidje 2016, Algorithm [18]).

Returns a tuple of `(solution, diagnostics)` where diagnostics contains
per-iteration τ, mass, timing, and rejection data for failure-mode analysis.
"""
function CommonSolve.solve(prob::FSPProblem{E,T}, alg::KrylovFSP) where {E,T}
    model = prob.model
    rates = prob.rates
    bc = prob.bc
    t0, tf = prob.tspan
    n_species = length(Tuple(prob.u0))

    # Initialize state space
    sp = StateSpace{E, Float64}()
    add_state!(sp, prob.u0, 1.0)

    # Solution storage
    sol_t = Float64[t0]
    sol_snaps = [(copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs))]
    sol_sizes = [length(sp)]

    # Diagnostics
    τ_log = Float64[]
    mass_log = Float64[]
    time_log = Float64[]
    walltime_log = Float64[]
    size_log = Int[]
    reject_count = 0

    # Lookback window for max-probability tracking
    prob_history = Vector{Dict{E,Float64}}()

    t = Float64(t0)
    τ = Float64(alg.τ_init)
    iter = 0
    wall_start = time()

    while t < tf && iter < alg.max_iter
        iter += 1

        # Determine pruning threshold
        threshold = alg.prob_threshold > 0 ? alg.prob_threshold : alg.ε / max(length(sp), 1)

        # Update lookback window
        current_probs = Dict{E,Float64}(s => sp.probs[sp.index[s]] for s in sp.states)
        push!(prob_history, current_probs)
        if length(prob_history) > alg.ℓ
            popfirst!(prob_history)
        end

        # Compute max probability over lookback window
        max_probs = Dict{E,Float64}()
        for hist in prob_history
            for (s, p) in hist
                max_probs[s] = max(get(max_probs, s, 0.0), p)
            end
        end

        # 1. Threshold prune (with lookback protection)
        prune_threshold!(sp, threshold; max_probs=max_probs)

        # 2. SSA-driven expansion
        expand_ssa!(sp, model, rates, t, bc; depth=1)

        # 3. r-step reachability expansion
        if alg.r > 0
            expand!(sp, model, bc; depth=alg.r)
        end

        # 4. Build generator + propagate
        τ_step = min(τ, tf - t)
        A, _, _ = build_generator(sp, model, rates, t)

        # Attempt matrix exponential; if it fails numerically, reject and halve τ
        local p_new
        expmv_ok = true
        try
            p_new = expmv(τ_step, A, sp.probs)
            if any(isnan, p_new) || any(isinf, p_new)
                expmv_ok = false
            end
        catch
            expmv_ok = false
        end

        if !expmv_ok
            # Treat as rejection
            τ /= 2
            reject_count += 1
            push!(τ_log, τ_step)
            push!(mass_log, NaN)
            push!(time_log, t)
            push!(walltime_log, time() - wall_start)
            push!(size_log, length(sp))
            continue
        end

        # Clamp small negative values from numerical noise
        @inbounds for i in eachindex(p_new)
            if p_new[i] < 0
                p_new[i] = 0.0
            end
        end

        # 5. Accept/reject based on mass conservation
        mass = sum(p_new)
        mass_target = 1.0 - alg.ε

        if mass >= mass_target
            # Accept step
            sp.probs = p_new
            t += τ_step

            push!(τ_log, τ_step)
            push!(mass_log, mass)
            push!(time_log, t)
            push!(walltime_log, time() - wall_start)
            push!(size_log, length(sp))

            # Save snapshot
            if iter % alg.save_interval == 0 || t >= tf
                push!(sol_t, t)
                push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
                push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
                @info "KrylovFSP: t = $(round(t; sigdigits=4)), |S| = $(length(sp)), τ = $(round(τ_step; sigdigits=3)), mass = $(round(mass; sigdigits=6))"
            end
        else
            # Reject: halve τ
            τ /= 2
            reject_count += 1

            push!(τ_log, τ_step)
            push!(mass_log, mass)
            push!(time_log, t)
            push!(walltime_log, time() - wall_start)
            push!(size_log, length(sp))

            if iter % alg.save_interval == 0
                @info "KrylovFSP REJECT: t = $(round(t; sigdigits=4)), τ = $(round(τ; sigdigits=3)), mass = $(round(mass; sigdigits=6))"
            end
        end
    end

    # Ensure final snapshot is captured (avoid duplicate if already saved in loop)
    if length(sol_t) == 1 || sol_t[end] < t - eps(t)
        push!(sol_t, t)
        push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
        push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
    end

    sol = FSPSolution{E}(sol_t, sol_snaps, sol_sizes, n_species)
    diag = KrylovFSPDiagnostics(τ_log, mass_log, time_log, walltime_log, size_log, reject_count, iter)

    (sol, diag)
end

using DiscStochSim, Catalyst, Random

rn = @reaction_network begin
    @species X(t) Y(t) Z(t)
    @parameters k1 k2 k3 k4 k5
    k1, Y --> X
    k2, X + Y --> 0
    k3, X --> 2X + Z
    k4, 2X --> 0
    k5, Z --> Y
end

y1s, y2s, y3s = 500.0, 1000.0, 2000.0
mu1s, mu2s = 2000.0, 50000.0

Random.default_rng(1)

    println("|S| range: [$(minimum(diag.size_log)), $(maximum(diag.size_log))]")

# Krylov-FSP-SSA vs AdaptiveFSP Comparison
# For reviewer response: demonstrates flux-aware pruning advantages
#
# Tier 1: Oregonator — full quantitative comparison
# Tier 2: Bottleneck — connectivity failure diagnostic
# Tier 3: Robertson — stiffness failure diagnostic

using DiscStochSim, Catalyst, Random, Printf
using Plots

gr()
default(
    fontfamily="Computer Modern",
    titlefontsize=14,
    guidefontsize=12,
    tickfontsize=10,
    legendfontsize=9,
    linewidth=2,
    framestyle=:box,
    grid=false,
    dpi=300,
)

const OUTDIR = joinpath(@__DIR__, "output", "comparison")
mkpath(OUTDIR)

# ============================================================================
# Tier 1: Oregonator — Full Quantitative Comparison
# ============================================================================
function run_oregonator_comparison()
    println("=" ^ 60)
    println("TIER 1: Oregonator — Full Quantitative Comparison")
    println("=" ^ 60)

    rn = @reaction_network begin
        @species X(t) Y(t) Z(t)
        @parameters k1 k2 k3 k4 k5
        k1, Y --> X
        k2, X + Y --> 0
        k3, X --> 2X + Z
        k4, 2X --> 0
        k5, Z --> Y
    end

    y1s, y2s, y3s = 500.0, 1000.0, 2000.0
    mu1s, mu2s = 2000.0, 50000.0
    rates = [
        mu1s / y2s,
        mu2s / (y1s * y2s),
        (mu1s + mu2s) / y1s,
        2 * mu1s / y1s^2,
        (mu1s + mu2s) / y3s,
    ]

    tfinal = 0.11
    prob = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(500, 1000, 2000), (0.0, tfinal), rates;
                      bounds=(0, 50_000))

    # Run AdaptiveFSP
    println("\nRunning AdaptiveFSP...")
    Random.default_rng(1)
    t_afsp_start = time()
    sol_afsp = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(
        ε_dt=1.0, prob_quantile=0.1, flux_tolerance=1.0,
        expansion_depth=1, save_interval=1000,
    ))
    t_afsp = time() - t_afsp_start
    traj_afsp = mean_trajectory(sol_afsp)

    # Run KrylovFSP
    # τ_init=1e-5 matches the natural time scale (AdaptiveFSP dt ≈ 6e-6)
    # max_iter=30000 caps runtime for feasibility
    println("\nRunning KrylovFSP...")
    Random.default_rng(1)
    t_kfsp_start = time()
    sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp = solve(prob, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-3, τ_init=1e-5, ℓ=5, r=1, save_interval=1000, max_iter=30000,
    ))
    t_kfsp = time() - t_kfsp_start
    traj_kfsp = mean_trajectory(sol_kfsp)

    # Print results table
    println("\n--- Oregonator Results ---")
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15s  %15s", "", "AdaptiveFSP", "KrylovFSP"))
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15.2f  %15.2f", "Wall time (s)", t_afsp, t_kfsp))
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15d  %15d", "Snapshots", length(sol_afsp), length(sol_kfsp)))
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15d  %15d", "Final |S|",
            sol_afsp.state_space_sizes[end], sol_kfsp.state_space_sizes[end]))
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15d  %15d", "Max |S|",
            maximum(sol_afsp.state_space_sizes), maximum(sol_kfsp.state_space_sizes)))
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15d", "KrylovFSP rejections", diag_kfsp.reject_count))
    println(@sprintf("%-25s  %15d", "KrylovFSP total iters", diag_kfsp.total_iters))

    # Generate plots
    # (a) Mean trajectories overlaid
    p1 = plot(title="(a) Mean trajectories", xlabel="Time", ylabel="Population")
    plot!(p1, sol_afsp.t, traj_afsp[:, 1], label="X (AdaptiveFSP)", color=:blue, linestyle=:solid)
    plot!(p1, sol_afsp.t, traj_afsp[:, 2], label="Y (AdaptiveFSP)", color=:red, linestyle=:solid)
    plot!(p1, sol_afsp.t, traj_afsp[:, 3], label="Z (AdaptiveFSP)", color=:green, linestyle=:solid)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p1, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 1], label="X (KrylovFSP)", color=:blue, linestyle=:dash)
        plot!(p1, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 2], label="Y (KrylovFSP)", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
        plot!(p1, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 3], label="Z (KrylovFSP)", color=:green, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    # (b) State space size over time
    p2 = plot(title="(b) State space size", xlabel="Time", ylabel="|S|")
    plot!(p2, sol_afsp.t, sol_afsp.state_space_sizes, label="AdaptiveFSP", color=:blue)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p2, sol_kfsp.t, sol_kfsp.state_space_sizes, label="KrylovFSP", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    # (c) dt/τ over time
    p3 = plot(title="(c) Time step size", xlabel="Time", ylabel="dt / τ", yscale=:log10)
    if length(sol_afsp.t) > 1
        dt_afsp = diff(sol_afsp.t)
        plot!(p3, sol_afsp.t[2:end], dt_afsp, label="AdaptiveFSP dt", color=:blue)
    end
    if length(diag_kfsp.τ_log) > 0
        plot!(p3, diag_kfsp.time_log, diag_kfsp.τ_log, label="KrylovFSP τ", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    # (d) Marginal distribution at final time
    p4 = plot(title="(d) Marginal P(X) at t_f", xlabel="X", ylabel="Probability")
    if length(sol_afsp) > 0
        m_afsp = marginal(sol_afsp, length(sol_afsp), 1)
        bar!(p4, m_afsp.values, m_afsp.probs, label="AdaptiveFSP", alpha=0.5, color=:blue)
    end
    if length(sol_kfsp) > 0
        m_kfsp = marginal(sol_kfsp, length(sol_kfsp), 1)
        bar!(p4, m_kfsp.values, m_kfsp.probs, label="KrylovFSP", alpha=0.5, color=:red)
    end

    fig = plot(p1, p2, p3, p4; layout=(2, 2), size=(1200, 800), margin=5Plots.mm)
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "oregonator_comparison.png"))
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "oregonator_comparison.pdf"))
    println("Saved oregonator_comparison.{png,pdf}")

    return (sol_afsp=sol_afsp, sol_kfsp=sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp=diag_kfsp,
            t_afsp=t_afsp, t_kfsp=t_kfsp)
end

# ============================================================================
function run_bottleneck_comparison()
    println("\n" * "=" ^ 60)
    println("TIER 2: Bottleneck — Connectivity Failure Diagnostic")
    println("=" ^ 60)

    rn = @reaction_network begin
        k1, A --> B
        k2, B --> B + C
    end

    rates = [1e-6, 1e-1]
    bounds = (0, Int(1e11))
    prob = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(1, 0, 0), (0.0, 1e5), rates; bounds=bounds)

    # Run AdaptiveFSP (full, as reference)
    println("\nRunning AdaptiveFSP (reference)...")
    Random.default_rng(1)
    t_afsp_start = time()
    sol_afsp = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(
        ε_dt=1.0, prob_quantile=0.9, flux_tolerance=1e-6, save_interval=1000,
    ))
    t_afsp = time() - t_afsp_start
    traj_afsp = mean_trajectory(sol_afsp)
    println("  AdaptiveFSP: $(length(sol_afsp)) snapshots, $(round(t_afsp; digits=1))s")

    # Run KrylovFSP (capped iterations — diagnostic)
    println("\nRunning KrylovFSP (max_iter=500, diagnostic)...")
    Random.default_rng(1)
    t_kfsp_start = time()
    sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp = solve(prob, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-4, τ_init=1e3, ℓ=5, r=1, save_interval=100, max_iter=500,
    ))
    t_kfsp = time() - t_kfsp_start
    traj_kfsp = mean_trajectory(sol_kfsp)
    println("  KrylovFSP: $(diag_kfsp.total_iters) iters, $(diag_kfsp.reject_count) rejections")

    # Check if B=1 state was lost in KrylovFSP
    bottleneck_state = CartesianIndex(0, 1, 0)
    if length(sol_kfsp) > 0
        final_states_kfsp = sol_kfsp.snapshots[end][1]
        has_bottleneck = any(s -> s[2] >= 1, final_states_kfsp)
        println("  KrylovFSP has B>=1 state at end: $has_bottleneck")
    end

    # Check bottleneck presence in AdaptiveFSP
    if length(sol_afsp) > 0
        final_states_afsp = sol_afsp.snapshots[end][1]
        has_bottleneck_afsp = any(s -> s[2] >= 1, final_states_afsp)
        println("  AdaptiveFSP has B>=1 state at end: $has_bottleneck_afsp")
    end

    # Print results table
    println("\n--- Bottleneck Results ---")
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15s  %15s", "", "AdaptiveFSP", "KrylovFSP"))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.2f  %15.2f", "Wall time (s)", t_afsp, t_kfsp))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15d  %15d", "Snapshots", length(sol_afsp), length(sol_kfsp)))
    t_reached_afsp = sol_afsp.t[end]
    t_reached_kfsp = sol_kfsp.t[end]
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.2e  %15.2e", "Time reached", t_reached_afsp, t_reached_kfsp))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.4f  %15.4f", "Final <A>", traj_afsp[end, 1], traj_kfsp[end, 1]))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.4f  %15.4f", "Final <B>", traj_afsp[end, 2], traj_kfsp[end, 2]))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.4f  %15.4f", "Final <C>", traj_afsp[end, 3], traj_kfsp[end, 3]))

    # Generate plots
    # (a) Mean of C over time
    p1 = plot(title="(a) Mean C trajectory", xlabel="Time", ylabel="<C>")
    plot!(p1, sol_afsp.t, traj_afsp[:, 3], label="AdaptiveFSP", color=:blue, linewidth=2)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p1, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 3], label="KrylovFSP", color=:red,
              linestyle=:dash, linewidth=2)
    end

    # (b) Mean of B over time (shows bottleneck loss)
    p2 = plot(title="(b) Mean B trajectory", xlabel="Time", ylabel="<B>")
    plot!(p2, sol_afsp.t, traj_afsp[:, 2], label="AdaptiveFSP", color=:blue, linewidth=2)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p2, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 2], label="KrylovFSP", color=:red,
              linestyle=:dash, linewidth=2)
    end

    # (c) State space size
    p3 = plot(title="(c) State space size", xlabel="Time", ylabel="|S|")
    plot!(p3, sol_afsp.t, sol_afsp.state_space_sizes, label="AdaptiveFSP", color=:blue)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p3, sol_kfsp.t, sol_kfsp.state_space_sizes, label="KrylovFSP", color=:red, linestyle=:dash)
    end

    # (d) KrylovFSP diagnostics: τ and mass over iterations
    p4 = plot(title="(d) KrylovFSP diagnostics", xlabel="Iteration", ylabel="Value")
    if length(diag_kfsp.τ_log) > 0
        iters = 1:length(diag_kfsp.τ_log)
        plot!(p4, iters, diag_kfsp.τ_log, label="τ", color=:blue, yscale=:log10)
        plot!(twinx(p4), iters, diag_kfsp.mass_log, label="mass", color=:red,
              linestyle=:dash, ylabel="Mass", legend=:bottomright)
    end

    fig = plot(p1, p2, p3, p4; layout=(2, 2), size=(1200, 800), margin=5Plots.mm)
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "bottleneck_comparison.png"))
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "bottleneck_comparison.pdf"))
    println("Saved bottleneck_comparison.{png,pdf}")

    return (sol_afsp=sol_afsp, sol_kfsp=sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp=diag_kfsp)
end

# ============================================================================
# Tier 3: Robertson — Stiffness Failure Diagnostic
# ============================================================================
function run_robertson_comparison()
    println("\n" * "=" ^ 60)
    println("TIER 3: Robertson — Stiffness Failure Diagnostic")
    println("=" ^ 60)

    rn = @reaction_network begin
        k1, A --> B
        k2, 2B --> C + B
        k3, C + B --> A + C
    end

    rates = [0.04, 3e6, 1.0]
    bounds = (0, 100_001)
    prob = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(10_000, 0, 0), (0.0, 1e4), rates;
                      bounds=bounds)

    # Run AdaptiveFSP
    println("\nRunning AdaptiveFSP...")
    Random.default_rng(1)
    t_afsp_start = time()
    sol_afsp = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(
        ε_dt=0.01, prob_quantile=0.4, flux_tolerance=1e-9, save_interval=1000,
    ))
    t_afsp = time() - t_afsp_start
    traj_afsp = mean_trajectory(sol_afsp)
    println("  AdaptiveFSP: $(length(sol_afsp)) snapshots, $(round(t_afsp; digits=1))s")

    # Run KrylovFSP (capped — diagnostic)
    println("\nRunning KrylovFSP (max_iter=200, diagnostic)...")
    Random.default_rng(1)
    t_kfsp_start = time()
    sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp = solve(prob, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-4, τ_init=0.1, ℓ=5, r=1, save_interval=50, max_iter=200,
    ))
    t_kfsp = time() - t_kfsp_start
    traj_kfsp = mean_trajectory(sol_kfsp)
    println("  KrylovFSP: $(diag_kfsp.total_iters) iters, $(diag_kfsp.reject_count) rejections")

    # Compute extrapolated completion time
    t_reached = sol_kfsp.t[end]
    tf = 1e4
    if t_reached > 0 && t_kfsp > 0
        extrapolated = t_kfsp * (tf / t_reached)
    else
        extrapolated = Inf
    end

    # Print results table
    println("\n--- Robertson Results ---")
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15s  %15s", "", "AdaptiveFSP", "KrylovFSP"))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.2f  %15.2f", "Wall time (s)", t_afsp, t_kfsp))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15d  %15d", "Total iterations", length(sol_afsp.t)-1, diag_kfsp.total_iters))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15.2e  %15.2e", "Time reached", sol_afsp.t[end], t_reached))
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15s  %15d", "Rejections", "N/A", diag_kfsp.reject_count))
    if length(diag_kfsp.τ_log) > 0
        println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15s  %15.2e", "Final τ", "N/A", diag_kfsp.τ_log[end]))
    end
    println(@sprintf("%-30s  %15s  %15.2e", "Extrapolated completion (s)", "---", extrapolated))

    # Generate plots
    # (a) τ vs iteration (shows halving cascade)
    p1 = plot(title="(a) τ vs iteration", xlabel="Iteration", ylabel="τ", yscale=:log10)
    if length(diag_kfsp.τ_log) > 0
        plot!(p1, 1:length(diag_kfsp.τ_log), diag_kfsp.τ_log,
              label="KrylovFSP τ", color=:red, linewidth=2)
    end

    # (b) Simulated time reached vs wall time
    p2 = plot(title="(b) Simulated time vs wall time",
              xlabel="Wall time (s)", ylabel="Simulated time")
    if length(diag_kfsp.walltime_log) > 0
        plot!(p2, diag_kfsp.walltime_log, diag_kfsp.time_log,
              label="KrylovFSP", color=:red, linewidth=2)
    end
    # Show AdaptiveFSP final point for reference
    scatter!(p2, [t_afsp], [sol_afsp.t[end]], label="AdaptiveFSP (complete)",
             color=:blue, markersize=8, markershape=:star5)

    # (c) Mass conservation over iterations
    p3 = plot(title="(c) Probability mass", xlabel="Iteration", ylabel="Mass")
    if length(diag_kfsp.mass_log) > 0
        plot!(p3, 1:length(diag_kfsp.mass_log), diag_kfsp.mass_log,
              label="KrylovFSP mass", color=:red, linewidth=2)
    end

    # (d) State space size over iterations
    p4 = plot(title="(d) State space size", xlabel="Iteration", ylabel="|S|")
    if length(diag_kfsp.size_log) > 0
        plot!(p4, 1:length(diag_kfsp.size_log), diag_kfsp.size_log,
              label="KrylovFSP", color=:red, linewidth=2)
    end

    fig = plot(p1, p2, p3, p4; layout=(2, 2), size=(1200, 800), margin=5Plots.mm)
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "robertson_comparison.png"))
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "robertson_comparison.pdf"))
    println("Saved robertson_comparison.{png,pdf}")

    return (sol_afsp=sol_afsp, sol_kfsp=sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp=diag_kfsp)
end
